title: THE DAY THE SUN STOOD STILL

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: On the day the Lord gave the Amorites over to Israel, Joshua said to the Lord in the presence of Israel: "Sun, stand still over Gibeon, and you, moon, over the Valley of Aijalon." So the sun stood still, and the moon stopped, till the nation avenged itself on its enemies, as it is written in the Book of Jashar. The sun stopped in the middle of the sky and delayed going down about a full day. — Josh 10:12-13 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here is one of the most astonishing moments in all of Scripture. In the middle of the battle, Joshua does something extraordinary. Before the whole nation, he speaks a bold command in the Lord's presence: "Sun, stand still." And amazingly, the sun stopped, and the day was lengthened so Israel could complete the victory. However exactly we understand what happened that day, the Bible presents it as a real and mighty act of God in answer to Joshua's prayer.

What strikes us first is the boldness of Joshua's faith. He asked for something utterly impossible by human reckoning. Yet he asked, out loud, in front of everyone, because he believed the God of Israel was greater than the sun and moon themselves. This was not reckless presumption; it was faith in the God who made the heavens and rules over them. Joshua's God was not limited by the ordinary workings of creation.

There is deep encouragement here about the greatness of our God and the boldness He invites in prayer. We often pray timid, small prayers, quietly assuming certain things are simply impossible. Joshua reminds us that we serve the Creator of the sun and moon, for whom nothing is too hard. "Is anything too hard for the Lord?" (Gen 18:14).

This does not mean God grants every bold request as we wish; He answers according to His wisdom and purpose. But it does mean we can come to Him with big, believing prayers, trusting a God of limitless power. In Christ, we are invited to "approach God's throne of grace with confidence" (Heb 4:16). The God who stopped the sun for Joshua is the God who hears us still.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are your prayers timid and small, or bold and believing?
2. What "impossible" thing have you assumed not even to ask God about?
3. How does the greatness of our Creator God shape the way you pray?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You made the sun and moon and rule over all creation. Give me bold, believing faith to bring big prayers to You, trusting that nothing is too hard for You. Amen.
